subject: History
description: Integration of states, major wars, economic reforms, political milestones 1947-2000

questions.stem: The INTEGRATION of princely states into the Indian Union after 1947 was carried out primarily by:
questions.explanation: Sardar Patel, as India's first Home Minister and Minister of States, with V. P. Menon as secretary, integrated 562 princely states. Junagadh (plebiscite 1948), Hyderabad (Police Action — Operation Polo, 1948), and Kashmir (accession October 1947) were the three hardest.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The STATES REORGANISATION ACT of 1956 created states primarily on the basis of:
questions.explanation: Following the Fazal Ali Commission (SRC, 1953-55) report, the 1956 Act redrew state boundaries along linguistic lines. Result: 14 states and 6 Union Territories. Earlier, in 1953, Andhra had already been created from Madras after Potti Sreeramulu's fast-unto-death. Later splits: Maharashtra-Gujarat (1960), Punjab-Haryana (1966), etc.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The year of India's first NUCLEAR test (Smiling Buddha) at Pokhran was:
questions.explanation: Pokhran-I (codename Smiling Buddha), 18 May 1974. Described by India as a 'peaceful nuclear explosion'. Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti), 11-13 May 1998, under Vajpayee's government — five tests that brought sanctions, later lifted under the 2008 US-India civil nuclear deal.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the WAR with its YEAR. A. Sino-Indian War. B. Indo-Pak War (creation of Bangladesh). C. Kargil War. D. First Indo-Pak War (Kashmir). List-II: 1. 1947-48. 2. 1962. 3. 1971. 4. 1999.
questions.explanation: 1947-48: First Indo-Pak war over Kashmir; UN-brokered ceasefire January 1949. 1962: India lost to China in Ladakh/NEFA. 1971: India-Pakistan war → Bangladesh liberation. 1999: Kargil war — India regained Kargil heights.

questions.stem: India's LIBERALISATION, PRIVATISATION and GLOBALISATION (LPG) reforms were initiated in 1991 under:

options.option_text: P. V. Narasimha Rao as PM and Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister

questions.explanation: The 1991 BoP crisis (with forex reserves low enough for only ~2 weeks of imports) forced structural reforms: rupee devaluation, industrial delicensing, trade liberalisation, opening to FDI. Manmohan Singh's 24 July 1991 Budget speech is often called the beginning of the 'new economy'.

questions.stem: The GREEN REVOLUTION in India was led by:
questions.explanation: M. S. Swaminathan, agricultural scientist, led the HYV (high-yielding variety) seeds + chemical fertiliser + irrigation push from mid-1960s. Worked with Norman Borlaug. Effect: wheat output doubled in Punjab-Haryana-western UP by 1970. Verghese Kurien led the WHITE REVOLUTION (Operation Flood — milk).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the EMERGENCY in India (1975-77). 1. Declared by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on PM Indira Gandhi's advice on 25 June 1975. 2. Triggered by the Allahabad HC judgment in Raj Narain vs Indira Gandhi. 3. Fundamental Rights were suspended under Article 359. 4. It ended formally on 21 March 1977 after the general elections. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Article 352 emergency was proclaimed on 'internal disturbance' grounds; the 44th Amendment (1978) later narrowed this to 'armed rebellion'. Shah Commission documented its excesses. Janata Party won 1977 election decisively, ending 30 years of Congress rule at the Centre.
